catalyst.event: Post-midterm regulatory repricing: rate-regulated utilities re-rate relative to merchant power as state-level data-center permitting risk is priced in
catalyst.action: existing position opened 2026-11-02 at 43.30 — hold, levels unchanged

thesis: This is an UPDATE to the open position opened 2026-11-02 at 43.30, not a new idea; levels are unchanged and the hold is being re-affirmed on new information. On 2026-11-04 the Democratic midterm sweep crushed merchant power generators (VST -13.8%, NRG -13.5%, TLN -8.5%, CEG -6.7%, GEV -9.3%) on data-center moratorium risk, while XLU closed +0.44% at 43.61. Rate-regulated utilities earn a return on approved rate base rather than on merchant spark spreads, so state-level hostility to new data centers does not reach their earnings the way it reaches an IPP.
key_risk: The 10-year at 4.95% against 3.88% fed funds is a steepening tape, and utilities are the most duration-sensitive equity sector — a further term-premium move takes XLU down regardless of the regulatory story.
counter_argument: If the post-election bid is really a flight into bond-proxy defensives, it unwinds as soon as the risk-on tape (SPY +1.65% the same session) reasserts, and XLU gives back the move without the regulatory re-rating ever happening.

evidence.detail: Close 43.61 sits above a rising SMA20 of 42.37 and SMA50 of 41.78; 6-month range high is 46.625, which is where the target is anchored, and the 41.80 stop sits below the SMA50. ATR14 0.6075 (1.39%), so the 1.50 stop distance is 2.47 ATR, clear of the 1.8 ATR ETF floor.

Measured one-day relative strength on the election reprice: XLU +0.44% versus VST -13.8%, NRG -13.5%, GEV -9.3%, TLN -8.5%, CEG -6.7% — regulated and merchant power separated by 7 to 14 points in a single session, which is the market pricing the policy risk as merchant-specific.

catalyst.event: Tax-free separation into CVS Health and CVS Pharmacy completing H1 2028, a 2027 adjusted EPS floor of at least $8.65 (+13%), and a share repurchase resuming in Q4 2026 against $35B of deployable capital
catalyst.action: accumulate in thirds across the 76-81 zone; add under 73; next hard information is formal 2027 guidance on the Q4 call in February 2027

thesis: CVS reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.09 against a $1.667 consensus (+25.4%, the third consecutive beat above 15%), raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $8.20 from $7.90-8.10, raised operating cash flow guidance to at least $15.5B from at least $11.5B, guided 2027 adjusted EPS to at least $8.65, and announced a tax-free split into two investment-grade companies — and the stock closed down 12.5% at 79.96, which is 9.25x that 2027 floor. The operating result and the price moved in opposite directions, so the de-rating is the market pricing PBM and drug-pricing legislative risk after the Democratic midterm sweep onto Caremark, not pricing the earnings. This is taken as a long-term accumulation rather than a swing because the downside here is a valuation floor, not a level a stop can defend: the 2026-10-16 swing position in this name was gapped straight through its 85.40 stop on this very print.
key_risk: The Democratic sweep makes PBM reform legislation materially more likely, and Caremark sits inside the Health Services segment management has already guided to a 2027 trough — a statutory change to PBM rebate economics would hit the highest-margin piece of the company and is the one risk no operating beat answers.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is positioning rather than fundamentals: insiders sold $359.0M across nine transactions in the last six months with zero open-market purchases, and the stock sits roughly 12% below both its SMA20 (90.37) and SMA50 (90.82), so the accumulation is being started against the trend and against what the people inside the company did with their own shares. A second count against is that the split does not complete until H1 2028, which is a long time to hold a thesis whose main re-rating catalyst is that distant.

evidence.detail: Read the Q3 2026 release filed as Exhibit 99.1 to the 2026-11-04 8-K: adjusted EPS $2.09 vs $1.60, revenue $108.399B +5.4%, consolidated adjusted operating income $4,194M +21.2%, Health Care Benefits MBR 91.3% vs 92.8% (-150bps) with segment adjusted operating income $912M vs $314M, and FY26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $8.20 with operating cash flow raised to at least $15.5B from at least $11.5B.

Target is 13x the 2027 adjusted EPS floor of $8.65 given on the Q3 call = $112.45. 13x is defensible rather than heroic: the stock printed 110.68 inside the last 150 sessions on lower guidance, 13x forward is below the S&P multiple, and the $8.65 floor explicitly assumes no EPS accretion from the buyback resuming in Q4 2026 against $35B of deployable capital. The bear case is $66 — roughly 8.2x a flat, no-growth $8.00, which is below the 52-week low of 69.51 — giving reward-to-risk of 33.45/13.00 = 2.57 against the 2.5 long-term floor.

The bear case is that Health Services earnings keep eroding. Management put a number on it instead of asserting it away: Health Services adjusted operating income is guided to at least $7B in 2027 and named as the trough, with 340B declining y/y but largely stabilizing by the end of 2027 and now a smaller share of segment earnings. Separately, commercial premium revenue fell 16.9% because CVS has already exited the individual exchange business, so the ACA subsidy-cliff exposure that sits on peers is not on this balance sheet.

catalyst.event: Defence budget risk repriced by the Democratic midterm sweep — HII -4.08% and RTX -2.64% on 2026-11-04 — against a shipbuilding backlog that is appropriated years in advance
catalyst.action: hold the existing position toward 339.76; the amendment is a protective stop at 278.00, which this position has never carried

thesis: This is an UPDATE to the open position opened 2026-10-12 at 262.00, now 303.99 (+21.0%), and the only change is that it finally has a stop. The 2026-11-04 midterm result took HII down 4.08% alongside RTX -2.64% as the market priced defence appropriations risk under a Democratic sweep, which is a genuinely new headwind to a position already up 21% with no downside protection at all. 278.00 sits just below both the SMA20 of 281.68 and the SMA50 of 279.05 and is 2.37 ATR beneath the close on an ATR14 of 10.9665, so it is below the trend rather than inside the noise.
key_risk: Average dollar volume is $178M a day, the thinnest book of any open position here, so an appropriations headline can gap straight through 278.00 rather than trading to it — the stop reduces the exposure, it does not guarantee the exit price.
counter_argument: The strongest case against setting the stop at all is that naval shipbuilding revenue is appropriated years ahead and a change of Congress does not cancel a carrier, so 278.00 risks being taken out by a political headline that never touches the backlog — and the position is then flat on a thesis that was right. The stop is accepted anyway because a 21% gain with no downside level is not a position, it is a hope.

evidence.detail: Stop placed at 278.00, just under a rising SMA50 of 279.05 and SMA20 of 281.68 and 25.99 below the 303.99 close, which is 2.37 ATR on an ATR14 of 10.9665 — clear of the 2.0 ATR swing floor for a single stock. 150-day range 255.355-336.21, and the 339.76 target sits just above the range high.

Measured one-day move on the election reprice: HII -4.08% to 303.99 and RTX -2.64% to 198.43 on a session where SPY closed +1.65%, so defence underperformed the index by roughly 5 to 6 points on the policy news specifically rather than drifting with the tape.

catalyst.event: A reaffirmed 8%+ annual adjusted EPS compounding guide through 2032 off a 2025 base of $3.71, a 36.7 GW renewables backlog, and the Dominion Energy combination closing H2 2027 at a pro forma 9%+ growth rate — into a Congress that just turned friendlier to renewables while turning hostile to the merchant-power alternative
catalyst.action: DO NOT BUY AT THE MARKET. NEE closed 88.45 after a 7.7% four-session run and does not clear the long-term reward-to-risk floor there. Work a limit into the 78.50-81.50 zone, which is the SMA20/SMA50 cluster it just left; accumulate in thirds and add under 76

thesis: NextEra is the only large US company that is simultaneously the biggest regulated utility (FPL) and the biggest renewables developer, which makes it the one name that gains from both halves of the 2026-11-04 repricing rather than just one: a Democratic Congress is the most favourable policy regime renewables have had, and the same session that bid NEE 4.89% took merchant power down 7 to 14 points (VST -13.8%, NRG -13.5%, CEG -6.7%) on state-level data-center permitting hostility. Power demand is not going away because a statehouse blocked a gas plant, and the supply that remains politically buildable is disproportionately NextEra backlog. The recommendation is explicitly a limit below the market, because at 88.45 the valuation does not clear the floor and the only way to make it clear would be to raise the target.
key_risk: The 8% compounding guide runs through 2032 and the Dominion combination does not close until H2 2027, so this thesis is carried for years on management execution — an interest-rate regime with the 10-year at 4.95% raises the financing cost of every gigawatt in that 36.7 GW backlog, and a utility that funds growth with debt is where that bites first.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the entry never fills: NEE is 9.4% above its own 20-day mean after a policy move, leadership tends to persist, and a limit at 80.50 may simply watch the stock leave. That is accepted deliberately. The honest alternative — buying at 88.45 — gives reward-to-risk of 1.22 against a 2.5 floor, so the choice is a limit that may not fill or a trade that does not qualify, and the first is the correct one. A second count against: six-month relative return is still -7.28% versus SPY +4.49%, so one month of leadership is being extrapolated from a base that was de-rating.

evidence.detail: Q3 2026 results: adjusted EPS $1.24 against $1.1917 consensus, up $0.11 and 9.7% y/y with adjusted earnings up $244M; nine-month adjusted EPS +9.5%; renewables backlog 36.7 GW. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance held at $3.92-$4.02 with management targeting the high end despite an expected weaker Q4 wind resource, and the 8%-or-better annual adjusted EPS growth rate through 2032 off the 2025 base of $3.71 reaffirmed, with operating cash flow growth at or above it.

2029 adjusted EPS on the company own reaffirmed 8% compounding off the $3.71 2025 base = 3.71 x 1.08^4 = $5.05. At 22x, below NEE peak multiple and a premium justified by a regulated earnings base plus the largest US renewables development arm, that is $111. The bear case prices a missed guide: 4% compounding gives 2029 EPS of $4.34 and the multiple compresses to a plain-utility 16x = $70, which is below the 150-day low of 74.41. From the 80.50 entry that is 30.50/10.50 = 2.90 against the 2.5 long-term floor; from the 88.45 market price it is 1.22 and fails, which is why the entry is a limit.

The 78.50-81.50 entry zone is the SMA50 at 80.3526 and SMA20 at 80.853, which NEE traded at four sessions ago before running 82.14 to 88.45. ATR14 is 1.8989 (2.15%), so the zone is roughly 4 ATR below the close rather than a reflex discount, and the $70 bear case sits below the 150-day low of 74.41. Average dollar volume $1.17B a day.

Computed relative strength: NEE +13.57% over one month against SPY -1.58% (+15.15pp) and against sector peer XLU +5.95% (+7.62pp), so this is leadership rather than a laggard being caught — while six-month return of -7.28% versus SPY +4.49% shows the de-rating being recovered from rather than a crowded trade being joined. Analyst recommendation trend improving, 66.7% bullish with strong buys going 6 to 7 month over month. Insiders are effectively inactive: one $585,480 sale in six months and no open-market buys, which is neutral rather than a negative.

thesis: Ameresco is an energy-efficiency and renewables contractor with roughly a $1.1B market cap and $11.53M of average daily dollar volume, and it was the only name in the clean-energy complex that FELL on 2026-11-04 — down 4.62% to 21.25 while TAN rose 5.65%, ARRY 14.87%, SHLS 8.15% and FSLR 4.63% on the Democratic sweep of both chambers. The mechanism worth paying for is not the policy read, which is already in the sector price, but the insider record underneath it: four distinct insiders made thirteen open-market purchases over six months, $1,914,610 bought against $876,272 sold, with founder and CEO George P. Sakellaris paying 21.60 to 22.84 in late August — every one of those prices above where the stock closed yesterday.
key_risk: This is a sub-$2B company with a 6.72% ATR reporting in two sessions, and its most recent Q1 2026 print was a miss (-0.35 against -0.3022), so a bad number can take out the 17.00 stop on the gap rather than trading to it. Small caps in this sector fund project backlog with equity, so a secondary offering is a live way this thesis dies before the fundamentals settle it. The wait instruction is load-bearing, not a formality.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is yesterday itself: AMRC opened 23.15, traded to 23.73 and closed 21.25, so the market was handed the most favourable policy news this sector will get and used the strength to sell. A key reversal day on the news is normally the end of a move, not the start of one, and no insider print from August answers what the tape did yesterday. That is precisely why the entry is a limit 6% lower and placed after the earnings date rather than before it.

evidence.detail: Six-month insider record: 13 open-market purchases (Code P) by 4 distinct buyers totalling $1,914,609.66, against 7 sales totalling $876,272.08, for a net +$1,038,337.58.
